name: Lucy McBath
incumbencyStatus: incumbent (four terms, 2019-present; represented GA-06 2019-2023, GA-07 2023-2025, GA-06 2025-present following redistricting)

electionContext.districtNote: GA-06 redrawn as D+25 district after redistricting; McBath won 2024 general election with 74.7% of the vote
electionContext.statusNote: McBath filed exploratory committee for Georgia governor race in March 2025 then suspended that bid in March 2025 to focus on husband's cancer recovery. As of February 2026 she remains in the House seat and has not announced a 2026 congressional re-election campaign formally, though she continues serving her current term through January 2027. Filed H.R.7599 in February 2026.

biography.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Georgia 6th Congressional District (2025-present); previously GA-07 (2023-2025) and GA-06 (2019-2023)
priorRoles: National Spokesperson and Faith & Outreach Leader, Everytown for Gun Safety and Moms Demand Action (approx. 2013-2018)
Flight attendant, Delta Air Lines (30-year career through early 2010s)
Intern, Virginia State Senate office of Douglas Wilder (early 1980s)
biography.education: B.A. Political Science, Virginia State University (1982)
biography.personalBackground: Mother of Jordan Davis, a 17-year-old killed in the 'Loud Music Shooting' at a gas station in Jacksonville, Florida, on November 23, 2012. Two-time breast cancer survivor. Has experienced three miscarriages. Married to Curtis McBath (who underwent cancer surgery complications in 2025). Her son's murder was the catalyst for her transition from flight attendant to gun violence prevention advocate and ultimately to Congress.
committees: Committee on Education and Workforce (including Subcommittee on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions; Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development)
Committee on the Judiciary — Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Crime and Federal Government Surveillance (119th Congress, 2025-present)

statedPositions.quote: After her son Jordan Davis was shot and killed in Jacksonville, Florida in 2012, Lucy decided to dedicate the rest of her life to fighting for gun safety and continues to advocate for common sense gun violence prevention.
statedPositions.notes: This is her defining issue — co-founder motivation for her entire congressional career. Supports universal background checks, assault weapons ban, extreme risk protection orders.

statedPositions.quote: As a two-time breast cancer survivor who lives with pre-existing conditions, McBath supports proposals making it easier for more Georgians to get covered and to expand upon the Affordable Care Act.
statedPositions.notes: Explicitly supports ACA expansion, not Medicare for All. Supports Medicaid expansion in Georgia and lowering Medicare eligibility age to 55.

statedPositions.quote: McBath has made lowering student debt a priority and supports fully funding K-12 education and making public universities, vocational schools, and community colleges more affordable.
statedPositions.notes: Emphasis on fully funding public education; no explicit school choice position found on campaign site.

statedPositions.quote: McBath believes the science of climate change is conclusive and indisputable: humans are the principal cause of it and the planet is warming at an extremely alarming rate.
statedPositions.notes: Supports increased investment in sustainable/renewable energy and incentives for solar and other renewables.

statedPositions.quote: Lucy McBath strongly disagrees with the Citizens United decision and will support legislation to increase transparency of the campaign finance system.
She fought to pass the Equality Act, which would proscribe discrimination of LGBTQ individuals in several areas including in the workplace, housing, and credit and financial assistance.
cut red tape and update permitting and zoning to build four million homes in the next decade
statedPositions.notes: Part of New Democrat Coalition Affordability Agenda released February 2026. Supports loosening permitting and zoning to increase housing supply — a market-supply approach rather than purely subsidy-based. Also supports increased Low-Income Housing Tax Credit allocations.

statedPositions.quote: Affordability Agenda focusing on lowering five care costs that are too high: health care, housing, energy, family care, and household essentials like groceries.
statedPositions.notes: Unveiled with New Democrat Coalition February 11, 2026. Framed around cost reduction including promoting competition, supporting small businesses, and breaking down regulatory barriers.

votingRecord.attendanceRate: 98.2% (missed 65 of 3,625 roll call votes, January 2019 – February 2026; on par with median of 2.0% for serving members)
votingRecord.billsEnacted: 8 bills as primary sponsor enacted into law, including Stop Campus Hazing Act (H.R.5646) and Federal Prison Oversight Act (H.R.3019)
votingRecord.sponsorshipTopics: Education (31%), Labor and Employment (24%), Crime and Law Enforcement (17%), Families (7%), Health (7%), Agriculture and Food (7%), Government Operations (7%)

keyVotes.notes: First major federal gun safety legislation in nearly 30 years. McBath's Federal Extreme Risk Protection Order Act was incorporated into this package. House passed 234-193 on June 24, 2022; all 220 Democrats voted yes.
Includes McBath's measure to cap insulin costs and lower prescription drug prices. Also ~$369B in climate investments. Medicare drug price negotiation provision.

keyVotes.bill: George Floyd Justice in Policing Act (H.R.1280, 2021)
keyVotes.notes: Co-sponsored and voted for bill passed House 220-212 on March 3, 2021. Included ending qualified immunity, national police misconduct registry, banning chokeholds. Failed in Senate.

keyVotes.vote: Yes (co-sponsor, first official act as Member)
keyVotes.notes: Co-sponsoring this was her first official act as Member of Congress — universal background checks for all gun sales.
Codified abortion access protections federally in response to Dobbs decision.
Enshrines same-sex and interracial marriage protections into federal law.

NOTABLE DEVIATION: McBath was one of 48 Democrats who voted for this Republican-backed immigration enforcement bill (first bill of 119th Congress). She had voted NO on a prior version. Bill requires DHS to detain undocumented immigrants arrested for theft, burglary, assault on law enforcement, or crimes resulting in serious injury. AJC characterized her as one of 4 Georgia Democrats who flipped. Signals moderate positioning on immigration enforcement.

keyVotes.bill: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act / Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (2021)
keyVotes.vote: Yes (inferred from press releases touting funding secured for Georgia; announced over $73M for Georgia from the law)
keyVotes.notes: House passed 228-206 on Nov. 5, 2021. McBath was in the majority. Includes public transit and clean energy infrastructure investments.
keyVotes.confidence: medium — specific vote confirmed by context; individual vote page not directly fetched

keyVotes.bill: Ensuring Women's Right to Reproductive Freedom Act (2022)
keyVotes.notes: Prohibits criminalization of interstate travel to obtain an abortion.

keyVotes.bill: Affordable Insulin Now Act (incorporated in IRA, 2022)
keyVotes.notes: McBath was the lead sponsor; the bill capped insulin costs at $35/month for Medicare beneficiaries. Went into effect January 2023. Eli Lilly subsequently announced voluntary price cuts attributed to McBath's bill.

legislationIntroduced.bill: H.R.7599 — Federal Extreme Risk Protection Order Act of 2026
legislationIntroduced.notes: Allows family members, household members, and law enforcement to obtain ERPOs from federal courts. Nationwide access to red flag law mechanism. Supported by Everytown, Giffords, Brady United, Newtown Action Alliance.
Led House reintroduction alongside Sen. Adam Schiff. Over 100 original co-sponsors. Bans semi-automatic assault weapons and magazines holding 10+ rounds.

legislationIntroduced.bill: GOSAFE Act (Gas-Operated Semi-Automatic Firearms Exclusion Act, 2025)
legislationIntroduced.notes: Reintroduced April 9, 2025. Prohibits manufacture, sale, transfer of certain gas-operated semi-automatic weapons and high-capacity magazines (10+ rounds). Also bans machinegun conversion devices including bump stocks and Glock switches.
Extends $35/month insulin cap (currently Medicare-only) to all Americans with private insurance.

scorecards.notes: Very high environmental score. Consistent with her votes on IRA, Infrastructure Law. Slight variation from 96% may reflect missed votes or procedural differences.
Near-perfect labor voting record. Consistent with New Democrat Coalition membership but reflects that coalition's pro-worker voting despite its moderate reputation.
Perfect score on civil liberties. Consistent with George Floyd Act cosponsorship, reproductive rights votes, Equality Act support.

scorecards.grade: F (de facto — no grade issued; NRA has actively campaigned against her)
scorecards.notes: NRA does not publicly grade McBath given she is one of the nation's most prominent gun violence prevention advocates and former Everytown employee. Her 2018 election was characterized as 'a massive defeat for the NRA.' NRA president Carolyn Meadows made controversial comments dismissing her 2019 victory as due to her being a 'minority woman.'
Considered a top gun violence prevention champion. Her first act as congresswoman was co-sponsoring Brady-backed universal background check legislation.
Giffords endorses her and lists her as champion. Her FERPO Act is specifically backed by Giffords.
Lifetime Heritage Action score is 2%. Near-zero conservative scorecard reflects consistent voting against conservative priorities.
Very low ACU score consistent with progressive voting record.
Liberal Quotient of 80 in 2019 — strong but not perfect liberal alignment, consistent with her New Democrat Coalition centrist positioning on some issues.

Notably higher than most progressive Democrats (who score 0-30%). This 71% is consistent with her New Democrat Coalition membership. Reflects votes on business-friendly legislation including possibly some trade or regulatory measures. This is a moderate outlier compared to her other scorecards.

keyExchanges.notes: 12-question profile from original 2018 campaign; covers her motivation and personal story.

keyExchanges.quote: After which failed pregnancy should I have been imprisoned?
keyExchanges.notes: Powerful personal testimony on reproductive rights; she spoke about her three miscarriages and the danger of criminalizing pregnancy loss if abortion is banned.

keyExchanges.quote: We have never had a situation like this where the Republican Party, under the leadership of this President, has said, we are not willing to negotiate... we are not willing to come to the table and that this is take it or leave it. Even though they know that millions of Americans, people that they actually represent, are going to be drastically hurt by the loss of their health care.
keyExchanges.notes: During government shutdown over ACA tax credit expiration. McBath strongly insisted subsidies must be included in any deal.
McBath defended Democratic position that ACA subsidies must be extended as part of any government funding deal. Said her constituents understand why Democratic senators are holding the line.

keyExchanges.quote: Georgians deserve a Governor who understands what's at stake — because they've lived it. As a mom and breast cancer survivor, I've seen firsthand how regular people are too often left out of the political process.
keyExchanges.notes: Statement when forming exploratory committee in March 2025. Subsequently suspended the committee in late March 2025 due to husband Curtis McBath's cancer surgery complications. Has not formally ruled out a future governor's race.

firearms_policy.summary: McBath is one of the most prominent gun violence prevention advocates in Congress. Gun safety is her defining legislative issue — it brought her to politics after her son Jordan Davis was shot and killed in 2012. She is the Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Federal Government Surveillance.
explicitPositions: Universal background checks for all gun sales (H.R.8 co-sponsor, first official act)
Assault weapons ban (H.R.3115, introduced April 2025)
Federal Extreme Risk Protection Orders / red flag laws (H.R.7599, introduced Feb 2026; ERPO included in Bipartisan Safer Communities Act 2022)
GOSAFE Act — banning gas-operated semi-automatic weapons and high-capacity magazines (10+ rounds), introduced April 2025
Banning machinegun conversion devices including bump stocks and Glock switches

No NRA rating — NRA considers her one of their top opponents

explicitPositions: Opposes Medicare for All / single-payer; supports incremental ACA improvements
Supports Medicaid expansion in Georgia (not yet adopted by state)
Supports lowering Medicare eligibility age to 55
Voted for Inflation Reduction Act (2022) which includes Medicare drug price negotiation
Led Affordable Insulin Now Act — $35/month cap for Medicare beneficiaries enacted 2023
Advocated for ACA subsidy extension during 2025 government shutdown
Supports extending $35 insulin cap to all Americans with private insurance (2025 bill)

Supports incentives for solar and other renewables for homeowners

labor_economy.summary: AFL-CIO score of 99% — essentially perfect labor voting record. Member of New Democrat Coalition which has moderate positioning but strong labor vote scores. Supports minimum wage increases (member coalition pushed longer timeline for Raise the Wage Act).

housing.summary: Released New Democrat Coalition Affordability Agenda (Feb 2026) with explicit support for loosening zoning and permitting to build 4 million homes over 10 years. Also supports increased Low-Income Housing Tax Credit. Market-supply-side framing rather than purely subsidy-based.
housing.confidence: medium — clearest recent statement is the Feb 2026 agenda; limited prior detailed housing record

police_justice.summary: ACLU score of 100%. Co-sponsored George Floyd Justice in Policing Act. Her personal history gives her a nuanced view — she supports accountability reforms while emphasizing that her advocacy for gun safety is about public safety. Ranking Member on House Crime Subcommittee.
police_justice.confidence: medium-high — ACLU score and George Floyd Act co-sponsorship are strong signals; she has not publicly addressed defunding/abolition

positionConflicts.conflict: McBath voted YES on the Laken Riley Act (Jan 2025), requiring mandatory detention of undocumented immigrants arrested for theft or burglary, after voting NO on a prior version. This is a significant rightward shift from her stated position of 'comprehensive immigration reform' and 'dignity and respect for all people.' She was among only 48 Democrats to support the first major bill of the Trump 119th Congress.

positionConflicts.topic: Chamber of Commerce score vs. progressive profile

This likely reflects New Democrat Coalition positioning on some business-friendly regulatory and trade votes. The Chamber score suggests her economic approach is more market-oriented than her labor/environmental record alone would indicate.

evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: high — seven-year House record provides strong multi-source evidence across most axes. Gaps are in housing (partially filled by Feb 2026 agenda) and specific school choice / sentencing positions.
evidenceSummary.notes: McBath's defining identity as a legislator is gun violence prevention. She is a moderate Democrat (New Democrat Coalition, not progressive caucus) who votes with labor and environmental groups nearly perfectly but takes more centrist positions on immigration enforcement (Laken Riley Act) and healthcare delivery (incremental ACA vs. Medicare for All). The unusually high Chamber of Commerce score (71%) is worth flagging for the scorer — it may reflect specific trade or regulatory votes. Her February 2026 housing agenda (cutting red tape, zoning reform, building 4M homes) signals a supply-side housing approach that partially overlaps with market-oriented framing.
